end.summary:
Named water vapour as a gas and ice as solid water.
Identified liquid water in rivers and water vapour in air.
Discussed evaporation, condensation, freezing, and melting using daily examples.
Explained that moving air can help wet clothes dry faster.
The idea that drying destroys water remained uncorrected at the last occurrence.
end.parentNote: Sana practised naming water as liquid, solid ice, and invisible water vapour, and used examples such as a freezer, wet clothes, and droplets on a cold glass. They explained that heat can turn water into vapour, that moving air helps clothes dry, and that droplets on a cold glass come from water in the air. One mix-up remained: they said the sun destroyed the water when clothes dried; at home, ask them to describe drying as water vapour going into the air rather than disappearing.
